messages:
emily_support: Hey team, customer ACME (acct acme-prod) reports a p99 latency jump after we flipped their model to the new int8 quant profile yesterday evening. They saw 95th ~220ms -> 300ms and p99 ~450ms -> 980ms. They attached a small repro and logs. Can we triage? :warning:

raj_runtime: Thanks Emily. Can you paste the exact toggle and model id they used? Also which region + deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private)?

emily_support: Hosted, region us-west-2. Model: rdlw-base-v2, variant: int8-profile-v4. Toggle command they used (from console audit): `api.toggle_model_variant(model_id=rdlw-base-v2, variant="int8-profile-v4", env="prod")`

lina_ml: Noted. Any sample request shapes? Sequence lengths and batch patterns matter a lot for int8 calibration.

emily_support: Customer shared two requests in the repro: short chat messages (avg 30 tokens) and occasional long generation (~1024 tokens). Their sample traffic interleaves them. They attached trace snippet: `p95: 310ms, p99: 980ms` and this block in runtime logs:
```
2024-07-15T18:12:03Z request_id=abc123 model=rdlw-base-v2 variant=int8-profile-v4 seq_len=1024 batch=1 kv_cache_hits=0 kernel=matmul_q8
2024-07-15T18:12:04Z request_id=abc124 model=rdlw-base-v2 variant=int8-profile-v4 seq_len=28 batch=8 kv_cache_hits=2 kernel=matmul_q8
2024-07-15T18:12:04Z lat_ms=980
```

kevin_oncall: Hypothesis: int8-profile-v4 calibration may have been built with mostly short sequences; when long sequences hit, kernel selection + KV cache behavior causes expensive path or memory copies, spiking p99. Also possible fallback to a slower kernel for certain seq_len thresholds.

raj_runtime: Agreed. Actions I propose: 1) reproduce locally against same variant + mixed seq distribution, 2) check kernel selection logs per request (we log selected kernel and reason), 3) temporarily rollback customer's route to fp16 variant while we investigate, 4) prepare a targeted canary for a tuned int8 profile.

emily_support: ACME asks for a timeline and temporary mitigation. They want rollback now if it's quick.

kevin_oncall: Emily, I can perform rollback in the console. Plan: set their route to `rdlw-base-v2-fp16` for the next 2 hours and monitor p99. Will notify before and after. Want me to proceed?

emily_support: Please proceed. Also add a note asking them to keep hitting the same repro payloads so we can capture logs.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Initiating route update for account acme-prod -> rdlw-base-v2-fp16 by kevin_oncall at 2024-07-15T18:40:12Z. Change-id: chg-7865.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Route update complete. New variant: rdlw-base-v2-fp16. Canary monitors: p50/p95/p99 enabled for 30m.

emily_support: ACME confirms p99 dropped to 420ms within 15m of rollback. They're still experiencing occasional spikes but much less severe. They asked if int8 can be tuned instead of staying on fp16 (cost concerns).

lina_ml: We should capture a full calibration profile using a representative mix of short+long sequences. Likely their calibration dataset lacked long-context samples, causing suboptimal kernel/packing decisions. Steps I want to run: 1) repro locally with a traffic generator that alternates short/long at same ratio, 2) run `quant-calibrate --model rdlw-base-v2 --dataset acme-sample-mix --out profile-int8-v4b --seq-buckets "[32,128,512,1024]"`, 3) run perf runs to measure p95/p99 across seq buckets.

raj_runtime: FYI, there is also a runtime knob `quant.fallback_policy`: values = [prefer_fp16, prefer_int8, auto]. For now we can set it to `auto` which triggers fallback to fp16 for requests that the runtime deems would be slower under int8. That could reduce p99 without full rollback. But it's a heavier CPU path and needs careful testing.

kevin_oncall: Can we toggle `quant.fallback_policy` per-route? If so, we could set `auto` for ACME and watch. That avoids a full variant switch.

raj_runtime: Yes per-route override exists. Command (internal): `redwood route update --acct acme-prod --route default --set "runtime.quant.fallback_policy=auto"`

emily_support: ACME prefers route override first, then switch to fp16 only if override doesn't help. They want clear rollback steps and an ETA for a tuned int8 profile.

lina_ml: ETA: I can run calibration + perf in ~3 hours if I get access to ACME's sample set (they already provided 2000 requests). I'll produce `profile-int8-v4b` and a comparison doc with p50/p95/p99 per-sequence-bucket. If we can automate a canary rollout (10% traffic) we can validate quickly.

kevin_oncall: I'll apply the `quant.fallback_policy=auto` override now and enable a 30m extended p99 monitor. If p99 doesn't improve within 20m, I'll revert to fp16 rollback we already used as plan B.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Route override applied for acme-prod: runtime.quant.fallback_policy=auto by kevin_oncall at 2024-07-15T19:02:10Z. Monitor window: 30m.

emily_support: ACME notes p99 dropped to ~460ms after override (improvement vs 980ms but slightly higher than pure fp16). They are okay with this temp state while Lina tunes.

lina_ml: Great. I'll start calibration runs now. Quick note on root cause hypothesis for the postmortem: mismatched calibration distribution + kernel tiling threshold that switches to a slower quantized matmul path for certain (seq_len, batch) combinations. Also possible inefficient KV-cache alignment under quantized kernels. Will include perf traces and kernel selection logs in the PM.

raj_runtime: Add to runbook: - how to set per-route `runtime.quant.fallback_policy` - how to rollback to fp16 - how to launch a canary for a new int8 profile - queries to pull kernel selection counts: `select count(*) from kernel_log where model='rdlw-base-v2' and variant like 'int8%' and kernel='matmul_q8_slow' and ts > X`

kevin_oncall: Action items assigned: Lina -> calibration + profile + canary by EOD (target 3h). Raj -> prepare automations to detect sequence-distribution-imbalances and warn on quant-profile toggles. Emily -> customer comms + confirm dataset access. I'll keep the override in place for now.

emily_support: I'll update ACME with the runbook and ETA, include the explanation for why longer sequences caused the regression, and that we have a remediation plan. Thanks everyone. :heart:

jane_customer: Thanks team, appreciate the fast response. We'll keep the repro traffic coming and share more samples if useful.

lina_ml: I'll post the perf comparison artifacts in this thread when ready and link the canary plan.

kevin_oncall: Logging this as internal incident: INC-2024-4219 (quant-int8-p99-acme) so we can track RCA and billing adjustments if needed.

emily_support: Closing loop for now — keeping thread open until Lina posts artifacts.
